blocks.name: Core practical 12: investigating magnetic fields
blocks.definition: Core practical 12: investigate the magnetic field pattern for a permanent bar magnet and between two bar magnets

blocks.md: - To investigate the magnetic field pattern for a permanent bar magnet and between two bar magnets

| **Equipment** | **Purpose** |
|---|---|
| Two bar magnets | Produce a magnetic field which is plotted |
| Plotting compasses | Show the direction of the magnetic field at a given point |
| Paper | Plot the magnetic field pattern on this |
| Pencil | Plot the magnetic field pattern with this |

- Place the magnet on top of a piece of paper
- Draw a dot at one end of the magnet (near its corner)

blocks.alt: Direction of Magnetic field Step 1, downloadable IGCSE & GCSE Physics revision notes

blocks.md:
- Place a plotting compass next to the dot, so that one end of the needle of the compass points away from the dot
- Use a pencil to draw a new dot at the other side of the compass needle

blocks.alt: Direction of Magnetic field Step 2, downloadable IGCSE & GCSE Physics revision notes

blocks.md: - Move the compass so that it points away from the new dot, and repeat the process above

blocks.alt: Direction of Magnetic field Step 3, downloadable IGCSE & GCSE Physics revision notes

blocks.md:
- Keep repeating the previous process until there is a chain of dots going from one end of the magnet to the other
- Then remove the compass, and link the dots using a smooth curve – this will be the magnetic field line

blocks.alt: Direction of Magnetic field Step 4, downloadable IGCSE & GCSE Physics revision notes

blocks.md: - Repeat the whole process several times to create several other magnetic field lines

blocks.alt: Direction of Magnetic field Step 5, downloadable IGCSE & GCSE Physics revision notes

blocks.md: - Repeat the whole process for two bar magnets placed 5 cm apart first facing the same pole then facing opposite poles

blocks.md: ***The magnetic field of a bar magnet plotted***

blocks.md: ***Magnetic field of two bar magnets interacting***

- Make sure the pencil you use is sharp to provide a clear and accurate drawing of the field lines
- Read the marker on the compass from above and not at an angle
- Allow the compasses to settle for a couple of seconds before taking the reading
